_about: 3-10, re-flown on wave 4c-2's build (WALL, step 175: a destroyable stone dies at the first wall it breaks, so the stone that used to
break this wall, fall on knight B and crush it at the ramp, leaving the key free for the player to take, is gone with the wall). This
is a different solution and it uses FOUR portals, two pairs: the stone crushes the knight on the wall, and the player goes through a
second pair after the key, which the dead knight leaves hanging where he stood.
The first walk is the old one's: left off the start platform from tick 28 to 196, down the ramp onto lift_ent_1318 (the player stands
on it at x 107.9; he must be on it between about x 89 and 122, the lift being 64 to 128 wide) and a touch on it (200, "shot": false)
sends it up (lift_sent 201). The lift is at its top from ~370, the player's centre at y 126.4. Knight B (minion_spawn_913) took
key_ent_1271 on tick 78 and stands from ~290 on the wall's left end at (276.6, 128.4), holding its 15 s at wayB1 (that hold is why
the whole job can wait there). From the top a shot at (276, 45), over the vertical block single_block_plat_1275 (its top corner is
at y 106 and the aim line clears it by about 5; tap 358, fired on 359; 326 to 384 win; it opens its portal on 412) and a shot at
(55, 96), at the rolling_stone_1198 that rests on the block beside him (tap 436, fired on 437; 412 to 452 win; it opens on 450 and
the stone goes in at once, traversal 450) bring the stone out over the knight: it falls onto him and crushes him on 463 (G1b: a
hit above 1.23), is not stopped, breaks the wall on 469 at 3.67 m/s against the gate's 1.5 and is destroyed with it (WALL). The
pair was spent by the stone. The key has no carrier now and hangs at (276.6, 117.3) over the hole in the floor (a key is a position
and an owner, never a body: Keys.hpp).
Second pair: a shot at (276, 48), again over the block (tap 478, fired on 479; 462 to 496 win; it opens on 530), and a shot at (108, 114),
a point in the player's own head room, 12 above the lift's top (tap 548, fired on 549; 530 to 560 win; it opens on 550 over the
player, who goes in at once, traversal 550, and comes out at the first, (276, 48), his y turned back: the exit is the partner's own
point, no offset, decoded 'invert'). He falls 270 px down the hole, passing within 26 of the key (taken on 559; the route wins for
an aim x of this shot within 24 of 276), takes the two crystals at x 272 on the way (561, 564) and lands on the ramp on 577 (hit 13.6, not
a death). The lift is sent down by a touch on it from where he is, after he has gone (tap 562; 550 to 576 win); it is at its foot
on ~728. He waits on the ramp and walks left from 650 (594 to 666 win: a walk started before 594, traced from 590, takes him off the ramp's top
into the shaft while the lift is still above it, and he falls to his death on 690), up the ramp, onto the lift as it settles, over it
and onto the block to the keyhole; the key trailing him is
within 26 of keyhole_ent_1196 on ~765 (unlock sound 767; the walk is held to 776, where he is against the wall; 760 to 836 win) and
flies in on 809; keyhole and door_locked_ent_1195 are gone on 859. He turns at once (777; 761 to 837 win, the door being gone
long before he is at x 355), walks down the ramp past the empty doorway and into the door: won on tick 943.
Leans on: WALL (the stone dies at the wall; the wall breaks at 3.67 m/s), G1b's crush of a knight by a stone, the key's pickup by the
player within 26 of it, R23's tap rules (the first shot's head-height retry fires on 359 with a drift of 0.96 px), a portal opened
over a body takes it in on its first tick, and G2's waiting lift. No knight sights or shoots him (the knight is dead before the
player is anywhere near its sight, and the run has no spot or shot line).
Unlocks no achievement: game/data/achievements.json has no level rule for 3-10 (the rules of world index 2 name levels 0 to 5, 7, 8,
10, 15, 20 to 23 and 31, not 9); the door line reads medal 3, 4 portals and 15.1 s. Not measured on the original: that a stone
dropped from a portal above the knight crushes him before it breaks the wall (it does on this build: the crush callback is decoded,
the order of the two contacts is the engine's), that a key whose carrier is dead stays where he stood, in the air, for the player to
take, and that the knight still stands at wayB1 at ~460 (its 15 s hold from ~290 is the port's timing). If the original's key falls
or the knight leaves, the designed solution differs and this is a route for the port's rules. Margins, from a scan that moved every
tap and walk edge by up to 40 ticks and each aim point by up to 30 units, one at a time: the aim points pass at 20 either way or
more, the taps have 12 ticks or more (the least are the lift tap's 12 early and the shot over the player's 12 late), the second
walk and the turn 16 or more, and the least are 6, on the first walk's start (28 within 20 to 34) and end (196 within 190 to 204),
which set where he stands on the lift, as in the old route.
